distIconIntroLegal:
A mark says only what this device read from the remote system, which can be wrong or out of date, and identifies neither a derivative, a rebuild, nor any particular version. Where it cannot be identified, a plain icon is drawn.

Each mark is a trademark of its respective owner and is used only to refer to the system it identifies.
distIconTip: Show a small mark beside each server for the system it appears to be running.
distNameMapTip: Only for a distribution whose file is named something else where you host the marks. The key is the name this app uses; the value is the name to fetch. Leave it empty unless a mark is missing.
dockerEmptyRunningItems:
There are no running containers.
This could be because:
- The Docker installation user is not the same as the username configured within the App.
- The environment variable DOCKER_HOST was not read correctly. You can get it by running `echo $DOCKER_HOST` in the terminal.

homeTabsCustomizeDesc: Customize which tabs appear on the home page and their order
hostCertAuthoritiesTip: A host whose certificate one of these signed is trusted without asking, as OpenSSH's @cert-authority; other hosts are asked about on first connection, as before. legacyStatusGoneBody:
The watch app and home widgets used to read a `/status` address typed by hand. That endpoint is gone: it could only report current values as text, which is why they could never show a chart.

They now read the Monitor's authenticated API, so they draw trends and stay in step with the app on their own. Configure the server in the app once, and every watch and widget picks it up.

monitorHttpTip:
Read this server's status from the **Monitor**'s HTTP API instead of running commands over SSH.

The Monitor has to be installed on the server first, and it is what makes trends, the watch app and the home-screen widgets possible.

[Setting up the Monitor]({url})

monitorLiveDevicesTip: Forgetting a device makes its next sign-in count against the account-wide limit on failed attempts. It does not sign the device out: a device that has the password signs in again. Change the password to keep a device out.

monitorPasswordNotSaved: The password was changed on the Monitor, but the app could not save it. Update this server's Monitor password in its settings.
monitorRelayForbidden: The Monitor refused this connection: its password has changed, or it does not act over plain HTTP. Sign in again, or connect over HTTPS.

pveTokenTip: Create one in PVE under Datacenter → Permissions → API Tokens. It needs VM.Audit, VM.PowerMgmt, VM.Console, VM.Snapshot, VM.Snapshot.Rollback, Datastore.Audit and Sys.Audit on the paths to show; with privilege separation on, grant them to the token itself.
pveTokenTipBackup: Cloning needs VM.Clone, backing up and restoring VM.Backup, and turning a guest into a template VM.Allocate; backup jobs also need Sys.Audit to read them and Sys.Modify on / to make, edit and delete them, with Datastore.AllocateSpace where the copy or the backup goes.
pveTokenTipCreate: Creating and deleting guests also needs VM.Allocate, VM.Config.*, Datastore.AllocateSpace and SDN.Use.
pveTokenTipHardware: Editing hardware needs VM.Config.CPU, VM.Config.Memory, VM.Config.Disk, VM.Config.CDROM, VM.Config.Network and VM.Config.Options; new disks and interfaces also need Datastore.AllocateSpace and SDN.Use. The video card and USB and PCI devices also need VM.Config.HWType; a device given through a resource mapping needs Mapping.Use on it, and Mapping.Audit to list mappings.
pveTokenTipStorage: Managing storage needs Datastore.Allocate on /storage (adding, disabling, removing), Datastore.AllocateSpace (volumes) and Datastore.AllocateTemplate (uploads); Linux bridges and applying the network configuration need Sys.Modify on the node.

remoteDesktopHostInvalid: The target host cannot contain spaces or line breaks.
remoteDesktopNameInvalid: The profile name can be up to 64 characters and cannot contain line breaks.
remoteDesktopSavePasswordTip: Stored in the encrypted database. Backups include saved passwords, and are encrypted only when a backup password is set.
remoteDesktopTargetTip: The target is resolved from the SSH server or the Monitor. Localhost refers to that machine.
remoteDesktopUniqueName: Profile names must be unique for this server.
remoteDesktopVncClipboardLatin1Only: VNC clipboard supports Latin-1 text only.
remoteDesktopVncPasswordAscii: Classic VNC passwords must contain ASCII characters only.
remoteDesktopVncPasswordHint: Classic VNC uses only the first 8 characters
remoteSessionIdleTimeoutTip: How long a remote desktop or a guest's console stays connected after you leave it. Before it closes, a notice gives you 10 seconds to keep it.
ruleTip: Metric: cpu / memory / swap / disk / network / temperature. Matcher: cpu0 for one core, used / free / avail for memory, rx / tx for network; disk and temperature ignore it. Threshold: a comparator and a value, such as >=80%, >=70c or >10m/s.
sameIdServerExist: A server with the same ID already exists
scheduledTaskEmptyFmt: No scheduled tasks for {user}. What is added here is written into that account's crontab.
scheduledTaskEnableNowTip: Off writes the line commented out.
scheduledTaskLinuxOnly: Scheduled task management currently supports Linux servers.
scheduledTaskPreserveTip: Comments, environment variables, and unrecognized lines in this crontab are preserved.
scheduledTaskUnavailable: crontab is not available on this server.
schemaTooNewBody: It was written by a newer version of ServerBox (storage v{stored}). This version reads up to v{supported}; nothing has been changed.
schemaTooNewPlainWarn: The file will contain every SSH private key, server password and API key in plain text. Anyone who gets the file can access them all.
schemaTooNewReinstall: Reinstall the newer version to open all your data again.
schemaTooNewTitle: This data is newer than the app
schemaTooNewWipeConfirm: All servers, keys, snippets and settings on this device will be deleted. This cannot be undone. A backup exported here would be the only copy left.
schemaTooNewWipeDone: Data deleted. Open the app again to start fresh.
schemaTooNewWipeFailed: Some of the data could not be deleted, and this build still cannot open what is left. Reinstall the newer version to reach it.
searchServerTip: Search by server name or address.
serverFilesUnavailableTip: Needs SSH to this server, or the Monitor installed with its file API on.
serverOverviewTip: Show the summary at the top of the server list, and the row of servers above an open one
serverTabConnBadge: Connection count on the server tab
serverTabConnBadgeTip: How many servers are connected, such as 2/4
serverUnreachable: Could not run a command on this server
serviceDetailsUnavailableTip: The service list is usable, but the manager did not return all status or startup information.
serviceJournalUnreadable: This account cannot read the journal
serviceManagerUnsupportedTip: This server uses a service manager that ServerBox does not support yet. Supported managers: systemd, procd, and OpenRC.
serviceOtherUnits: {count, plural, one{1 other unit} other{{count} other units}}
sftpEditorTip: Empty uses the built-in editor. For example `vim` (reading `EDITOR` is suggested).
sftpRmrDirSummary: Use `rm -r` to delete a folder in SFTP.
sftpUnavailableUseScp: If this host has no SFTP subsystem, as many embedded devices do not, set its file transfer to SCP in the server settings.
shareCodeHint: Tell the recipient these digits separately. They are not included in the QR code.
shareExpired: This share has expired. Ask for a new one.
shareIncludesKey: The share includes the private key.
shareOmittedBmc: BMC credentials. The address is included, but the credentials are not.
shareOmittedJump: The jump server, because it is stored as a separate server on this device.
shareOmittedKeyPath: The key file, because its path is only valid on this device.
shareOmittedMissingKey: The private key, because it is not in this device’s key store.
shareOmittedTip: Not included; the recipient must configure:
sharePassphraseTip: This passphrase encrypts the file. The recipient needs it to import the server, and it cannot be recovered.
shareQrTip: The connection details in this QR code are encrypted. The share expires in {minutes} minutes.
shareServerExists: “{name}” on this device already uses this address. Import anyway?
shareTooBigForQr: Too large for a QR code. Share it as a file instead.
shareTooNew: This share was created with a newer version of ServerBox. Update the app to open it.
shareUnreadable: This is not a valid ServerBox share.
sharingClientsHint: Who may mount it: * for anyone, a host, an address or a network such as 192.168.1.0/24.
sharingConnectionsLinuxOnly: Sharing management currently supports Linux servers.
sharingDuplicate: Another share has this name or folder.
sharingFolderHint: A folder on the server, e.g. a disk mounted in Storage.
sharingGuestLabel: Let anyone on the network in without an account
sharingInstallNfsBody: Installs the NFS server with the machine's package manager.
sharingInstallSambaBody: Installs Samba with the machine's package manager.
sharingInvalidClient: A client is *, a host, an address or a network.
sharingInvalidName: A name is letters, digits, _ . - (32 at most).
sharingInvalidPath: The folder must be an absolute path without quotes, backslashes or ..
sharingNoNfs: The NFS server is not installed. Linux and macOS mount NFS exports.
sharingNoSamba: Samba is not installed. Windows, macOS and Linux open SMB shares.
sharingNotAFolder: {path} is not a folder on the server.
sharingPasswordsBody: Samba keeps its own passwords: set one for each account that connects.
sharingRefused: The configuration was refused and the previous one is back: {detail}
sharingRemoveNfsBody: Stops exporting {path}. The folder and its files stay.
sharingRemoveSmbBody: Stops sharing {name}. The folder and its files stay.
sharingSaveNfsBody: Exports {path} over NFS, then reloads the exports.
sharingSaveSmbBody: Shares {path} over SMB as {name}, then reloads Samba.
sharingShowConnectionsBody: Reads who is connected, as root.
sharingUsersHint: Accounts allowed in (none ticked: every account with an SMB password):
sizeTooLargeOnlyPrefix: Content too large, displaying only the first {bytes}
specifyDevTip: Network traffic counts every device by default; name one here instead
sshAdvancedTip: ProxyCommand, jump server, file transport, remote path
sshFileTransportTip: SFTP suits anything current. Choose SCP for an old or embedded host whose SSH server has no SFTP subsystem: it needs the `scp` command and a shell that also has the usual file utilities (`find`, `stat`, `mv`, `chmod`).
sshHostKeyChangedDesc: The SSH host key changed for {serverName}. Only continue if you trust this server.
sshHostKeyNewDesc: A new SSH host key was received from {serverName}. Review the fingerprint before trusting.
sshKeyLockedFmt: The private key [{name}] was not unlocked.
sshKeyPassphraseTip: Optional. A key with a passphrase is stored encrypted, and you are asked for it the first time a connection uses the key.
sshKeyPublicKeyTip: Append this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server.
sshKeyUnlockTip: Enter the passphrase for the private key [{name}].
sshKnownHostKeysTip: The host keys this app has accepted
sshLegacyAlgorithmsTip: For an old SSH daemon (a router, a switch) that only offers the SHA-1 `ssh-rsa` host key or a SHA-1 key exchange. Less secure; turn it on only for a host that needs it.
sshTcpForwardingProhibited: The SSH server refused to forward this connection. Check AllowTcpForwarding and PermitOpen in its sshd_config, and any no-port-forwarding or permitopen option on the key in authorized_keys.
sshTermHelp: When the terminal is scrollable, dragging horizontally can select text. Clicking the keyboard button turns the keyboard on/off. The file icon opens the current path SFTP. The clipboard button copies the content when text is selected, and pastes content from the clipboard into the terminal when no text is selected and there is content on the clipboard. The code icon pastes code snippets into the terminal and executes them.
statusCollectionTip: Which commands run, custom commands, which device to read
storageAddMemberBody: Adds {device} to /dev/{array}: it replaces a failed member, or waits as a spare. What it holds is lost.
storageAddSpareBody: Adds {devices} to pool {name} as spares. What they hold is lost.
storageAddToPoolBody: Adds {layout} of {devices} to pool {name} for more room. They cannot be taken out again, and what they hold is lost.
storageAttachBody: Mirrors {existing} onto {replacement}. What {replacement} holds is lost.
storageBusy: Another change to the disks is running.
storageConfirmationMismatch: The confirmation text did not match.
storageCreatePoolBody: Builds pool {name} ({layout}) from {devices}. Everything on them is lost.
storageCreateRaidBody: Builds /dev/{name} (RAID {level}) from {devices}. Everything on them is lost.
storageDeleteRaidBody: Stops /dev/{array} and wipes its members' RAID signatures. Its data is lost.
storageDestroyPoolBody: Destroys pool {name} and everything in it.
storageExpandBody: Grows the filesystem on {device} to fill its device. It stays mounted.
storageFormatBody: Makes a new filesystem on {device}. Everything on it is lost.
storageGrowPartitionBody: Grows {device} into the free space after it. Expand its filesystem after.
storageGrowRaidBody: Adds {device} to /dev/{array} as one more working member. RAID 1 gains a mirror; RAID 5 and 6 gain room once the reshape ends, which can take hours. Expand its filesystem after. What {device} holds is lost.
storageInitializeBody: Wipes {device} and gives it one partition for the whole disk. Everything on it is lost.
storageInvalidDevice: The device is invalid or no longer available.
storageInvalidLevel: The RAID level or pool layout is invalid.
storageInvalidPassphrase: The passphrase must be 8 to 512 characters, on one line.
storageLinuxOnly: Storage management currently supports Linux servers.
storageLockBody: Closes {device}. Its filesystem must be unmounted.
storageNeedsSudo: sudo asked for a password: run the Monitor as root, or allow these commands (above).
storageNoMdadm: mdadm is not installed: arrays cannot be built or changed here.
storageNotGrowable: This device cannot be grown here.
storageNotMounted: Nothing is mounted there any more.
storageNotRemovable: Only a spare or cache device can be taken out here.
storageOnlineBody: Brings {device} back into pool {name}, grown into the whole disk.
storageOverlapping: Choose devices that do not overlap.
storagePassphraseHint: At least 8 characters. Without it the data cannot be read: keep it safe.
storagePickDevices: Pick at least {count} devices. What they hold is lost.
storageRemoveMemberBody: Marks {device} failed and takes it out of /dev/{array}. The array runs on without it, degraded if it was a working member.
storageReplaceBody: Replaces {old} in pool {name} with {replacement}. The pool copies its data onto it; what {replacement} holds is lost.
storageScrubBody: Reads all of pool {name} and repairs what it can. It runs in the background.
storageSmartLongTestBody: Starts a long self-test on {device}. It reads the whole disk: hours on a large one.
storageSmartTestBody: Starts a short self-test on {device}. It takes a few minutes; its progress and result show here.
storageSystemMount: The system uses this mount; it stays mounted.
storageTooFewDevices: Not enough valid devices were selected.
storageUnmountBody: Unmounts {mountpoint} and stops mounting it at start.
storeKeyLostAsk: The key that encrypts ServerBox's data is not in the system keystore. If the keystore or keyring is only unavailable right now, for example not yet unlocked, try again. Otherwise ServerBox can start with no data; the old file is kept.
storeUnreadableKeyLost: The key that encrypts ServerBox's data is no longer in the system keystore. This happens when the system resets the keystore, when the keyring service is not available, or when the app's data was copied from another device, for example by a phone migration tool. The data cannot be decrypted without that key, so ServerBox started with no data.
storeUnreadableKeyRejected: The key in the system keystore does not open ServerBox's data: the data was encrypted with another key, or the file is damaged. ServerBox started with no data.
storeUnreadableTitle: Previous data could not be opened
storeUnreadableVaultFailed: The system keystore could not decrypt the key that encrypts ServerBox's data, so ServerBox reset the keystore entries and started with no data. The backup password, the WebDAV and GitHub credentials and the saved sudo passwords have to be entered again.
storeVaultFailedAsk: The system keystore could not decrypt the key that encrypts ServerBox's data. If the keystore failed only this once, try again, if needed after restarting the device. If it fails every time, the data cannot be decrypted, and ServerBox can start with no data; the old file is kept. Starting with no data also clears the backup password, the WebDAV and GitHub credentials and the saved sudo passwords.
storeVaultFailedRootHint: On a rooted device, a module that intercepts the keystore (such as TrickyStore) causes this. Remove this app from the module's target list, then start with no data.
sudoPromptNotFound: No sudo password prompt is active.
supportFmtArgs: The following formatting parameters are supported:
suspendTip: The suspend function requires root permission and systemd support.
syncPasswordMismatch: Synced data is encrypted with a different backup password. Enter the backup password used on your other devices.
syncRemoteTooNew: Synced data was created by a newer version of ServerBox. Update the app to continue syncing.
syncSwitchBody: Auto sync with {name} will be turned off. Existing backups on {name} will not be deleted.
syncUnreachable: Could not connect to the sync service. Check your network connection and try again.
systemdUserScopeMissingTip: This account has no user session bus on the server, so only system units are shown.
tagEditorTip: Typing filters the list; the button creates the tag and puts it on this server in one step. Renaming from the pencil renames it on every server that carries it. A tag no server carries disappears on save.
tagsEmptyTip: No tags yet. Add one while editing a server and it will appear here.
tcpTargetUnreachable: The server could not connect to this address. Check that the service is running and listening on that port.
tempIsCelsiusTip: When enabled, the temperature value will be treated as Celsius instead of millicelsius. Turn on only if the temperature displays incorrectly (e.g., showing 0.1°C instead of 58°C).
termFontSizeTip: This setting will affect the terminal size (width and height). You can zoom in on the terminal page to adjust the font size of the current session.
termInFloatWindow: This terminal is in the floating window
termLineHeightTip: The space a terminal row takes, as a multiple of the font size, from 1.0 to 2.0. Like the font size, it changes how many rows fit.
termMetricsBarTip: CPU, memory, network and disk, as the server card shows them. Above the virtual keys on a phone.
textScalerTip: 1.0 => 100% (original size), only works on server page part of the font, not recommended to change.
transportNoneOn: Enable at least one connection method.
transportSectionOff: Off. The fields below are kept for when you turn it back on.
userManagerLinuxOnly: System user management currently supports Linux servers.
userMoveHome: Move the existing home directory when the path changes
userPasswordCreateTip: Leave the password empty to create a password-locked account.
userPasswordEditTip: Leave the password empty to keep the existing password.
userRootChangesWarning: Changes to root take effect in every session at once.
versionUnknownUpdate: Current: v1.0.{build}, click to check updates
versionUpdated: Current: v1.0.{build}, is up to date
virtBackupExcludeTip: Every guest on the node is taken. Turn one off to leave it out.
virtBackupIssueNodeOffline: The job's node is not online.
virtBackupIssueOption: Not a mode or compression PVE takes.
virtBackupIssueStorage: That storage does not hold backups on this node.
virtBackupJobDeleteAsk: Delete the backup job {id}? The backups it made stay.
virtBackupJobsNone: No scheduled backup job. Add one to back guests up on a schedule.
virtBackupModeStops: suspend and stop interrupt a running guest while it is copied.
virtBackupNoPlan: No scheduled backup job takes this guest.
virtBackupNoStorage: No storage on this node holds backups.
virtBackupNotesTemplateTip: The notes are added to each backup the job makes. These are replaced by their values: {vars}.
virtBackupPlanNewTip: A schedule that backs up this guest alone.
virtBackupPlanOthers: {count, plural, =0{No other guest} =1{Also backs up 1 other guest} other{Also backs up {count} other guests}}
virtBackupProtectTip: A protected backup is kept from pruning and cannot be deleted until protection is removed.
virtBackupProtected: Protected: it cannot be deleted until protection is removed in PVE.
virtBackupPruneTip: PVE's retention options, e.g. keep-last=7,keep-daily=4. Empty: the storage's or the node's own.
virtBackupRestoreAgain: The guest's disks and configuration are replaced by the backup's.
virtBackupScheduleHelp: A subset of systemd calendar events: 02:30, mon..fri 02:30, sat 03:00, daily, hourly, */15.
virtBackupScheduleInvalid: Not a schedule the host takes.
virtBackupStoppedTip: Stopped: backed up as it is
virtCiAddressInvalid: An IPv4 address with its prefix, like 10.0.0.5/24
virtCiCredentialsMissing: Set a password or an SSH key.
virtCiDnsInvalid: IP addresses, separated by spaces or commas
virtCiEditTip: What cloud-init sets up in this VM: an account with sudo, how to log in to it, the hostname and the address.
virtCiEffectLibvirt: Saving writes a new seed with a new instance ID.
virtCiEffectPve: PVE writes its cloud-init drive at once, with an instance ID derived from these settings, so any change here makes a new one.
virtCiEffectTitle: Takes effect at the next boot
virtCiExpireNote: The first login with it has to set a new one. libvirt only: PVE writes "expire: false" and has no option for it.
virtCiForeignBody: Settings made elsewhere (packages, commands, other accounts) are not shown here. Saving replaces the seed with what is shown.
virtCiForeignTitle: This seed holds more than this app writes
virtCiHostnamePve: The hostname is the VM's name.
virtCiKeysAdded: Keys are added to the account. A key taken out here stays in the system until it is removed there, and a new user name makes a new account beside the old one.
virtCiNewInstance: At the next boot cloud-init treats the system as a new instance: it sets the hostname again, makes the account if it is missing, sets its password, adds the keys and writes the network configuration again. It also makes new SSH host keys, so SSH clients warn that the host key changed. Nothing changes before that boot.
virtCiNicsTip: {count} NICs in the seed's network config; the form edits the first.
virtCiNoToolBody: Install one of {tools} on the host. Without cloud-init the image starts with no account to log in with.
virtCiNoToolTitle: No tool on the host to make the cloud-init data
virtCiPasswordKept: Set. Leave empty to keep it
virtCiRemovePasswordNote: Log in with an SSH key only
virtCiSaved: Saved. It takes effect at the next boot.
virtCiSearchTip: Several, separated by a space; resolv.conf keeps the first few.
virtCiSeedNote: Written to a small ISO next to the disk, attached as a CD-ROM and deleted with the VM. Only the password's hash is stored.
virtCiTip: An account with sudo, logged in to with its password, an SSH key, or both.
virtCiUserInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, starting with a letter or _
virtCloneEmptyNote: Off: new empty disks of the same size
virtCloneFullOnly: Only a template can be cloned as a linked clone
virtCloneLinkedNote: Off: a linked clone, which depends on the template's disks
virtCloneLinkedTarget: A linked clone shares the template's disks, so it cannot name a storage or a node.
virtCloneNodeUnknown: This host has no such node.
virtCloneStorageContent: This storage does not hold VM images.
virtCloneStorageMissing: No storage on this node holds VM images.
virtCloneStorageShared: Copying to another node needs a shared storage.
virtCloudImageTip: A disk with a system on it: copied, grown to the size under Storage, and set up by cloud-init at its first boot. The image itself is left as it is.
virtConsoleAutoEnter: Pressing Enter in {seconds, plural, =1{1 second} other{{seconds} seconds}} to bring up the prompt
virtConsoleNone: No console is configured for this guest
virtConsoleSerialTip: Opens the guest's serial console with virsh on the host. Disconnect, or Ctrl+], returns to the host's shell.
virtCreateCoresInvalid: More cores than this host allows.
virtCreateCredentialsMissing: Set a root password or an SSH key.
virtCreateDiskKept: The disk was kept at {size}, the image's own size, which is more than was asked for: a disk is never cut below the system on it.
virtCreateImageBigger: The image is bigger than the disk: make the disk at least as big.
virtCreateImageSize: The image is {size}: the disk must be at least that big.
virtCreateIncomplete: Complete the parts marked orange first.
virtCreateKindLxcSub: pct · shares the host's kernel, lighter
virtCreateKindVmSub: qm · a full KVM virtual machine
virtCreateMediaMissing: That install media is not on this host.
virtCreateNameInvalidLibvirt: Letters, digits, ., _ and -, starting with a letter or digit; up to 63 characters.
virtCreateNameInvalidPve: Letters, digits and -, in parts separated by dots; up to 63 characters.
virtCreateNameTaken: A guest with this name exists.
virtCreateNetworkMissing: A new guest cannot use that network.
virtCreateNotOffered: This host does not offer that for a new VM.
virtCreateSecureBootNote: Only signed kernels and bootloaders are booted.
virtCreateSshKeysInvalid: One OpenSSH public key per line.
virtCreateWindowsBody: Choose UEFI and turn the TPM on above.
virtCreateWindowsNoTpm: This host has no software TPM (swtpm): install it to give the guest one.
virtCreatedNotStarted: {name} was created but did not start
virtCredentialsTip: A root password, SSH keys, or both.
virtDeleteDisksPve: Its disks are deleted with it; install media is kept.
virtErrConflictTip: Someone changed this configuration after it was read here, so nothing was changed. It has been read again: make the change again if it still applies.
virtErrExecNotGranted: The Monitor does not run commands
virtErrExists: A guest or disk with this name already exists
virtErrInvalidResponse: The host answered in an unexpected form
virtErrNotConfigured: The PVE settings of this server are incomplete
virtErrNotConfiguredTip: Check the address, and the password or API token, in the server's settings.
virtErrNotInstalled: virsh is not installed on this server
virtErrRelayNotGranted: The Monitor does not open TCP connections from the server over this link
virtErrSudoRequired: sudo needs a password to reach libvirt
virtHwAppliesOnRestart: Saved. It takes effect at the next start.
virtHwBalloonNote: Lets the host take back the guest's idle memory when memory runs short
virtHwBiosSub: SeaBIOS · older systems and MBR disks
virtHwBootTip: The arrows move a device; tapping it switches booting from it on or off.
virtHwBusStopped: The bus changes only while the guest is stopped.
virtHwCdromLater: While it runs, the drive is added at its next start (SATA and IDE take none live).
virtHwCloudInitNote: What cloud-init reads at the first boot. Not install media: nothing to insert here.
virtHwDevicesEmpty: USB and PCI passthrough, CD-ROM, TPM
virtHwDiskHotplug: Hot-pluggable: can be added while it runs
virtHwFirmwareStopped: The firmware changes only while the guest is stopped.
virtHwFirmwareWarnBody: Switching between UEFI and BIOS leaves an installed system unable to boot.
virtHwFirmwareWarnTitle: Don't switch the firmware of an installed system
virtHwGrowNote: Disks only grow from their size.
virtHwGrowNoteRunning: Disks only grow from their size. Grown while running, the partition has to be grown inside the guest.
virtHwHotplugNow: Hot-plugged: it takes effect at once.
virtHwIommuOffBody: Turn on VT-d or AMD-Vi in the host's BIOS and IOMMU in its kernel first. Until then, a guest given a PCI device won't start.
virtHwIommuShared: {count} devices share its IOMMU group and are passed through together
virtHwIssueCpuOnline: Online vCPUs: from 1 to the total
virtHwIssueDiskShrink: Larger than it is: disks only grow
virtHwIssueMac: Must be a unicast MAC address, such as 52:54:00:12:34:56
virtHwIssueStorageMissing: Pick a storage for it first
virtHwIssueStorageSpace: More than the storage has free
virtHwLinkNote: Off, the guest sees its cable pulled; no restart needed
virtHwListenAllBody: Listening on all addresses lets anyone who can reach the host connect to the console. Keep 127.0.0.1 and connect through an SSH tunnel.
virtHwListenAllTitle: The console is open to the network
virtHwMappingsOnly: Only resource mappings can be used here: PVE lets only root@pam, signed in with its password, pass a raw device through. Create mappings under Datacenter → Resource Mappings.
virtHwMountFromPool: Mount points are allocated straight from a storage
virtHwNoHostDevices: No devices to pass through on this host
virtHwPciBody: Once passed through, the host can't use the device, and the guest can't migrate while running.
virtHwPendingBanner: Some hardware changes take effect at restart
virtHwPickPool: Pick a storage and a size
virtHwRevertAllAsk: Drop every change waiting for {name}'s next start?
virtHwRevertPendingBody: {name} is put back on what it is running: the definition is written again from the running one, and the next start gets exactly what this one has. Its NVRAM file and firmware stay as they are.
virtHwSecureBootNote: Boots only signed kernels and boot loaders
virtHwSecureBootVars: Turning Secure Boot on or off makes the EFI variables anew; boot entries saved in them are lost.
virtHwUefiSub: OVMF · Secure Boot capable, needed by Windows 11
virtHwVolumeKept: Removed, but the running guest still uses the disk, so its volume was kept. It is detached at the next start.
virtKeyHelpSnippet: Pick a snippet and run it in this terminal.
virtKeyHelpZellij: Manage Zellij sessions on the SSH host.
virtKeyIntroActionsTip: These open something instead of typing. Hold one to read what it does.
virtKeyIntroCustomizeTip: Reorder these keys, turn on more (the file browser, sudo, F1–F12…), or hide the ones you never reach for, in the terminal settings.
virtKeyIntroModifiersTip: Tap one to arm it, then tap a letter on the keyboard. It stays on for that one key.
virtKeyIntroNavTip: These move the cursor. Hold an arrow to repeat it.
virtKeyIntroSelect: Drag sideways over the terminal to select text, whenever it has something to scroll.
virtKeyRowsTip: The rest go on a page of their own, swiped sideways.
virtNetApplyAsk: Apply the pending network configuration on {node}? PVE reloads the host's network (ifreload -a): a mistake in it can cut the host off.
virtNetBridgedTip: Guests join a bridge of the host's, on its physical network
virtNetDeleteAsk: Delete the network {name}? It is stopped and its definition removed.
virtNetDeleteAskPve: Remove the bridge {name} from {node}? It leaves the pending configuration now, and the host once that is applied.
virtNetEditAsk: The running network keeps what it has until it is restarted. Restarting cuts off the {count} guests on it.
virtNetEditAskNoGuest: The running network keeps what it has until it is restarted.
virtNetEditPending: The definition has a change the running network is not on yet.
virtNetEditRestartNote: The guests on it lose their network while it restarts.
virtNetHostEmpty: No address is handed to a MAC of its own: every guest gets one from the DHCP range.
virtNetHostInvalid: A MAC, an address or a name the host would refuse, or the same MAC twice.
virtNetHostOthers: Every other guest gets one from the DHCP range.
virtNetInUse: Guests on it: {count}. It cannot be deleted.
virtNetInactivePve: Not active: a new bridge waits in the pending configuration until it is applied.
virtNetIsolatedTip: Only the guests and the host reach each other
virtNetManagementIface: This interface carries the host's own address. Editing or applying it would cut the host off.
virtNetManagementTip: It carries the host's management traffic, or sits under an interface that does: the app does not edit it.
virtNetNatTip: Through the host: guests reach out, nothing reaches in
virtNetPendingSaved: Saved as pending: apply the configuration for it to take effect
virtNetPendingTip: PVE keeps network changes in interfaces.new until they are applied.
virtNetPhysicalTip: A physical interface is the host's own: the app edits bridges only.
virtNetPortsHint: eno2; empty for an internal bridge
virtNetPveApplyNote: Saved as a pending change: it takes effect when the configuration is applied (ifreload -a).
virtNetRestartAsk: Restart {name}? The {count} guests on it lose their network until it is back.
virtNetRevertAsk: Drop the pending network configuration on {node}?
virtNetRoutedTip: Routed by the host without NAT: the LAN needs a route back
virtNetStopAsk: Stop {name}? The {count} guests on it lose their network until it starts again.
virtNetVlanTip: Guests' NICs may carry a VLAN tag
virtNoCloudImagesLibvirt: No cloud images here: put a qcow2 or raw image in a pool (upload it in Storage), one no guest uses.
virtNoCloudImagesPve: No cloud images here: upload a qcow2, raw or vmdk image to a storage with the Import content type (PVE 8.2+).
virtNoDiskStorage: Nowhere on this host takes a new disk
virtNoHostsTip: A server running Proxmox VE, with its API access filled in, is a host, and so is one where virsh answers. The other servers can be checked from the host switcher.
virtNoIsos: No ISO images on this host
virtNoTemplates: No container templates on this host. A storage's CT Templates in PVE can download one.
virtOffTip: Start it to see live CPU, memory, disk and network here.
virtPoolDeleteAsk: Remove the pool {name}? Its definition goes; its volumes stay where they are.
virtPoolDeleteKeepsVolumes: Its {count} volumes are kept on disk.
virtPoolDeleteStorage: Also delete its directory (only when empty)
virtPoolInUse: A guest uses a volume here, so the pool cannot be stopped or removed.
virtPoolInactive: The pool is not active, so its volumes cannot be listed.
virtPoolLogicalNote: An existing volume group is used as it is; nothing is formatted.
virtPoolStopAsk: Stop the pool {name}? Its volumes cannot be listed or created until it starts again.
virtProbeContainerTip: This server runs in a container, so it is a guest rather than a host. It is managed from the host that runs it.
virtPveSetupTip: {version} is running on this server. Fill in its API access in the server's settings (an API token is recommended) to manage its virtual machines and containers here.
virtResCidrInvalid: An address with its prefix, e.g. 192.168.150.1/24
virtResDhcpInvalid: Two addresses in the network, in order, without the host's own
virtResFormat: Not a format this pool holds
virtResNameInvalid: Not a name this host takes (letters, digits, . _ -)
virtResNotFound: It is no longer on this host
virtResSourceInvalid: Not a path or source the host takes
virtResSubnetTaken: Another network here is on this subnet
virtResUnsupported: This host does not do that
virtSbUnsupported: The host's firmware descriptors have no Secure Boot firmware with enrolled keys, so a domain with it cannot start.
virtSetDeleteProtected: Protection is on: turn it off under General first.
virtSetDeleteStopFirst: Shut it down before deleting it.
virtSetIssueDescription: At most {max} bytes (UTF-8), and no control characters.
virtSetProtectionNote: Blocks deleting the guest and changing its disks
virtSetRenameStopped: Shut the guest down to rename it: libvirt renames only a guest that is not running.
virtSnapshotDiffAsk: What changes if you revert to {snapshot}:
virtSnapshotDiffHost: The host could not say what differs: {error}
virtSnapshotDiffNone: The configuration is unchanged since this snapshot.
virtSnapshotExternalExists: The guest is already on {count} layers; this snapshot adds one more.
virtSnapshotExternalNoMemory: An external snapshot never holds the memory: the guest is not stopped.
virtSnapshotExternalTip: The guest keeps running. Each disk gets a qcow2 overlay in the chosen pool; the guest stays on a chain.
virtSnapshotMemoryAlways: A snapshot of a running guest always includes its memory here.
virtSnapshotMemoryOff: The guest is not running, so only its disks are saved.
virtSnapshotMemoryTip: Reverting resumes the guest at this moment.
virtSnapshotNameInvalid: A letter first, then letters, digits, - or _; 2 to 40 characters.
virtSnapshotNameTaken: A snapshot with this name exists.
virtSnapshotNoSupport: The guest's storage does not support snapshots, so none can be taken.
virtSnapshotRevertAsk: Revert {guest} to {snapshot}? Every change since it was taken is lost.
virtSnapshotRevertChain: Reverting on a chain merges the running overlay into the image and leaves every later snapshot unusable. Only the newest snapshot can be reverted to.
virtSnapshotRevertHasChildren: Refused while a later snapshot sits on this one.
virtSnapshotRevertStops: This snapshot has no memory: {guest} will be stopped.
virtSnapshotRevertTip: Reverting discards every change made since the snapshot.
virtStorageClusterWide: This applies to every node of the cluster that has this storage.
virtStorageDisableAsk: Disable the storage {name}? Guests with disks on it cannot start until it is enabled again.
virtStorageRemoveAsk: Remove the storage {name} from PVE's configuration? What is on it stays.
virtTemplateTip: A template only runs once it is cloned.
virtToTemplateIrreversible: This cannot be undone: a template cannot be turned back into a guest.
virtToTemplateNote: A template cannot be started and cannot be turned back into a guest. Its disks become base images, which is what a linked clone shares.
virtToTemplateSnapshots: A guest with snapshots cannot become a template.
virtUnprivilegedTip: Its root is an ordinary user on the host.
virtUsbAddressTip: The device follows this address: whatever is plugged there is given to the guest. libvirt names a USB hostdev by bus and device number.
virtVncPasswordNeeded: This display asks for a password
virtVolAttachNote: Attached as a new disk, on the bus its first disk is on
virtVolDeleteAsk: Delete the volume {name} from {pool}? What is in it is gone for good.
virtVolEmptyAttach: A new volume can be attached to any VM later
virtVolEmptyUpload: An ISO can also be uploaded directly
virtVolGrowFromGuest: A guest uses it: grow it from that guest's Hardware view
virtVolIsBase: Other volumes are made on this one; deleting it would break them
virtVolNone: This pool has no volumes yet.
virtVolPveName: PVE names a volume for its VM: vm-<VMID>-disk-<N>
waitConnection: Please wait for the connection to be established.
wolTip: After configuring WOL (Wake-on-LAN), a WOL request is sent each time the server is connected.
workspaceClosePaneHint: Closes every tab in it; can be undone
workspaceConnectHint: This server is set not to connect at launch.
workspaceEmptyTemplate: An empty workspace has no layout to save
workspaceNewTabFocused: New tab · in the focused pane
workspacePanesHead: {workspace} · two panes are shown; the tapped one gets focus
workspacePickView: New tab on {server} · choose a view
workspaceQuickOpenHead: Quick open · Enter opens the first
workspaceQuickOpenHint: Servers, views, tabs or workspaces, e.g. db docker
workspaceSeamTip: Drag to resize, double-click to even out
workspaceSyncBar: Sync input: typing goes to the {count} terminals of this workspace
workspaceSyncOnToast: Sync input on: typing in any terminal goes to every terminal of this workspace
workspaceTemplatesHead: Layout templates · new workspace on the focused pane's server
writeScriptFailTip: Writing to the script failed, possibly due to lack of permissions or the directory does not exist.
writeScriptTip:
After connecting to the server, a script will be written to `~/.config/server_box` 
 | `/tmp/server_box` to monitor the system status. You can review the script content.
zellijAutoTip: Automatically start or attach Zellij when connecting over SSH
zellijInvalidName: Enter a valid Zellij session name.
zellijSessionSelectorTip: Show the session picker when connecting
zellijTerminateConfirm: Terminate Zellij session “{name}” and its running programs?
